No readable source prints a latitude-first point for Markansaya: the English and Spanish Wikipedia articles carry no coordinates, the Mincetur inventory record 583 prints none, and the Datahub copy lists them longitude-first and about 4.5 km from the stored point.

The English Wikipedia article calls Qasr Chbib a complex of two Roman temples but gives no date, century or period for its construction, and no other readable source was found that dates it.
Wikipedia (en, es), the Inkaterra rock-art PDF and the academia paper give no date for the Intiyuq K'uchu paintings; no readable source dates the site.

No readable source prints a point for the ruins of Pukara on the Chivay-Coporaque road; the stored point coincides with the centre of the village of Coporaque (MINCETUR inventory), which is not the site, and Wikipedia carries no coordinates for the article.
No source readable by the checker dates the start of Pukara in Coporaque by year or century; Wikipedia lists only buildings, chullpa tombs, storehouses and walls without a date.

Wikipedia (en, es, fr), the MINCETUR-based travel pages and the Casaverde article abstract only call Inka Wasi (Incahuasi de Parinacochas, Pullo) an Inca site; no readable source states a year or century for its start.

Neither the English Wikipedia article nor the Wikidata item Q15950077 prints a coordinate for Qullqapampa; the article's infobox carries no coordinate and the item has no P625 statement, so no source gives a point for the site.
The English Wikipedia article names the culture only as Inca and gives no year, century or millennium for the site's construction or first occupation, so nothing dates its start.

No page prints a point for the Cloaca of Capri: neither the English or Norwegian Wikipedia article nor its Wikidata item (Q5134732, no P625) carries coordinates, and Commons and web searches found no register or article that does.
The only source, Wikipedia, says the sewer was 'built in Roman times'; that is a period word without a year, century or millennium for its start, and no other source on this sewer was found.
Neither Wikipedia (en, de), Wikidata (no P625) nor OpenStreetMap/Nominatim print a point for Said Qala Tepe, and no readable page found gives its coordinates.
No readable source dates the start of the Modi peak sanctuary; the pages found give only the general Minoan period of peak sanctuaries (a class), not a start for this site.

No readable source prints a point for Çimdin Kalesi itself: the Ministry's e-kitap page and the Cultural Inventory's record describe the castle and its monumental gate but carry no coordinates, OpenStreetMap has no record under either name (Çimdin or Çemdin Kalesi), and Wikidata has no item, so the stored point stays and the field goes to the owner.

Wikipedia gives no date; Beyond the Range says only that the site 'may have been used long before 1200 A.D.' and the Incas visited 500 years ago, and a travel page names the Inca Tupac Yupanqui without a year, so no source states a start year, century or millennium for Killarumiyoq.
The Wikidata item gives no inception or a date for the site, and the readable pages that mention the settlement print no year for its start, so no source dates the start of the settlement.

The Wikidata point (14°28'36"S, 70°38'14"W, no references) coincides with the town of Nuñoa, while the Mincetur inventory and a Universidad Nacional del Altiplano thesis place Maucallacta 15-18 km from Nuñoa (in the community of Kajsili); no source prints a usable point for the site itself.
The thesis and the Mincetur inventory describe rooms, circular enclosures and chullpas but name no single site type that a quotable word of the canonical type list supports; left for the owner.
The only description assigns the site to the Late Intermediate Period without any year or century; a period word alone does not date the start.

No readable source prints a point for the enclosure itself: the Wikipedia article and Wikidata item carry no coordinates, and the Historic England, Heritage Gateway, Abingdon town-council and Megalithic Portal pages are refused or script-built; the stored point is the centre of Abingdon-on-Thames, not the Radley Road site.

The only dated range readable by the checker is the DOAM 'Relative Chronology: 3500 BCE - 1800 BCE', which is a template for the whole 'Proto Historic' class (Mohenjo Daro carries the identical range); Wikipedia gives only the period word Mature Harappan and a radiocarbon sample date, and the Heritage of Sindh 2600-1800 B.C. page is behind a bot challenge.

No readable source prints a coordinate pair for Waruq: the English article has no coordinates at all and its Wikidata item Q17107672 carries no P625 statement, so the stored point stays and the site goes to the owner's list.

No source I could read dates the start of Waruq: the English article describes only its Quechua name and its location in Yarowilca Province, Huánuco, and gives no year, century or millennium, so the field stays empty.

Wikipedia and the MINCETUR record (Incaraccay, San Pedro de Cachora) only say the remains date from the Inca period (época Incaica); no source gives a year, century or millennium for the start of this site.

No readable source gives a point for ancient Lartos: Wikipedia has none, Pleiades gives only a rough Barrington Atlas box in the wrong part of the Aegean, and no readable page equates the ancient village with the modern village of Lardos. The stored point (the north tip of Rhodes) is far from the south-east coast, but no sourced replacement exists.
No source dates the ancient village of Lartos; the pages found concern modern Lardos and its medieval castle.

Sources call it a Buddhist stupa, which is not a canonical type; no readable source uses a word of a fitting canonical type (temple, monument, tomb, mound) for the structure itself, so the field stays empty.

The German Wikipedia article on Caklibel prints coordinates 36.454, 33.91575, but those are the hamlet's own point; its text says the ruins of Karaboculu lie near that village (Bei Caklibel liegen die Ruinen), so the pair is a village coordinate, not the site, and the stored point stays unsourced.

The English Wikipedia article on Caklibel (formerly Karaboculu) dates the ancient farm complex to the Roman and early Byzantine era, given as the range of the 3rd-5th centuries, and the German article says only that it was settled from the late Hellenistic to the early Byzantine period. Both are period ranges, not a single start year or the century word with a stated start, so the start is not dated here.

The only pages that name the Karaboculu ruins are the English and German Wikipedia articles about the neighbourhood of Caklibel, not about the archaeological site, and the Mersin government register that lists it is a PDF the checker cannot read.

The only printed point is the Wikipedia/Wikidata one (-14.413556, -74.170611), which lies on the namesake peak in Cabana District while the heritage resolution places the site in Aucara District; no independent source gives the site's own point.
No source found gives any date or period for Hatun Misapata.
English and Spanish Wikipedia and the CEAcusco project page call the Pampacolca (Castilla) complex Inca and give no year or century for its construction.
Neither the English article of the item nor its Wikidata item dates the site; the article gives only the region, province and district, so no source states a start year.
Sources only call Qhapaq Kancha an archaeological site of the Inca period; that is a period word with no year, century or millennium for its start.

The Roman milestones of Braga are a series of markers spread over several parishes of the municipality, and their Wikidata item carries no coordinate location at all, so no source prints a point that could be quoted and the stored point stays.

The St Fagans museum page dates only the Iron Age as a period ("The earliest and largest house was built during the Iron Age") and Coflein dates only the site's end ("The settlement is thought to have gone out of use during the late third or fourth century"). No source states a year, century or millennium for the start of the settlement, so the field stays empty.
